5 Narrow Sections  
5.2 Narrowing section without signed priority
5.2.1 Order of preference in the absence of road signs
The following explains the order of preference in the absence of road signs, signals or authorised persons, and applies to priority when different types of vehicles approach a narrow road section and it is necessary for one of the vehicles to reverse back to allow the other vehicle to pass. Under these circumstance priority is given as follows:
1.Special vehicles and those travelling under special regulations that exceed the established masses and dimensions as per the regulated rules of vehicles (MAM).
2. Set of vehicles-except those within point 4 below.
3. Vehicles pulled by animals.
4. Cars that tow a trailer of up to 750 kilograms MAM and camping vehicles.
5.Public transport vehicles-designed to transport passengers.
6. Lorries, tractive units and good vans and goods vehicles.
7. Car and vehicles derived from cars.
8. Special vehicles that do not exceed the mass or dimension established within the regulating laws; heavy quadricycles and light quadricycles.
9. Three wheeled vehicles, motorcycles with sidecar and three wheeled mopeds.
10. Motorcycles, two wheeled mopeds and bicycles.
(Página 209 del manual 'Learning to drive')

6.3 Emergencies
When a vehicle is forced to stop, due to unforeseen circumstances, on the railway crossing or on a mobile bridge (for instance due to a break-down or because their load has fallen off etc.,) the driver must get out of the vehicle and must endeavour to quickly evacuate all the occupants from the vehicle, and clear the crossing as rapidly as possible.
(Página 210 del manual 'Learning to drive')

6.1 Approaching
Drivers approaching a level crossing or moveable bridge must be extremely prudent and reduce their speed.
Users who find level crossings or moveable bridges closed or with the barrier or semi-barrier in motion when approaching should stop one after the other in the corresponding lane until they can pass.
(Página 210 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5 Narrow Sections    
5.3 Narrow bridges
Two vehicles that need special authorisation to travel may not cross a bridge at the same time if the width of the roadway is less than six metres, so that each vehicle may have a track width of not less than three metres. In the event of an encounter or crossing between such vehicles, the provisions of the preceding paragraphs shall apply.
(Página 210 del manual 'Learning to drive')

9 Immobilisation: Stationary vehicles Detention (Halting)
9.1 Definition - Concept
If a vehicle is detained – ‘halted’ inside a closed area for a period of time in excess of two minutes, the driver, although he should not leave the vehicle, must stop the engine and keep illuminated the position lights and if necessary the hazard warning lights.
(Página 196 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Priorities, level crossings and tunnels
 
7 Tunnels and underpasses
7.1 Stopping in tunnels or underpasses
If, whilst inside a tunnel or underpass, a vehicle is forced to stop due to traffic congestion and because of other stationary vehicles, the occupants of the vehicle mustn’t leave the vehicle. The driver must put on his hazard warning lights (temporarily) to inform the drivers that travel behind him of the situation. He should also keep illuminated the position lights (side lights) but turn off the engine. All drivers must stop as far as possible away from the vehicle in front -extend their safety distance.
(Página 211 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Tunnels and underpasses
7.1 Stopping in tunnels or underpasses
In the case of a fire, within a tunnel or underpass, the driver must position his vehicle to the far right side of the road, as close as possible, so as to not to obstruct the emergency service vehicles but allow them access. He should then, turn off the engine and leave the car keys in their place and the doors open.
The driver and all the occupants must leave and abandon the vehicle going quickly to the nearest shelter or exit, in the opposite direction to the fire. However, under no circumstances should they enter into the roadway or any other area that they are excluded from.
(Página 211 del manual 'Learning to drive')
